scope_clarifications.review: Used the general connected graded Noetherian-domain basis theorem; distinguished basis degrees from evaluation-index group weights; preserved the BoundarySheaf structure with a distinguished normalized vertex, with a greatest-vertex hypothesis added where the recognition theorems require it.

The displacement subgroup uses the original geometric action. The finite plane inversion count is defined before the induced Coxeter system and is later proved to equal intrinsic length. Relative intervals map monotonically and injectively into ambient intervals.

Polynomial.reflect reverses indices through d and fixes indices above d. Integer anti-reciprocity forces all coefficients above d and the possible middle coefficient to vanish, so the lowPart_solution theorem needs no separate degree hypothesis.

The generic dihedral polynomial theorem has no root-plane prerequisite. The induced-label structure model uses ambient roots and direct interpolation; its definition no longer records canonical P or P=1 as a proof dependency.
The actual nonnegativeAugmentation has codomain A and image A_0. The interpretation as a map to k uses the connected nonzero algebra identification.

Finite graded covers allow integer generator degrees and prove convergence for arbitrary ambient k-subspaces. The factor (1-q)^N removes the polynomial coefficient series, whereas (1-q) is the quotient factor for one regular degree-one scalar.
The reverse-projectivity application now follows the source explicit lifts and retraction, with the common image and regular scalar kernel constructed first.

Twist uses a general ring automorphism directly in the scalar action; identifying it with CoefficientChange for the inverse automorphism additionally uses preservation of the chosen base-field scalars.
The generic symmetric-algebra quotient and primality proof is separated from polynomial-coordinate transport and unit detection at a plane prime.

Trace restriction is proved for every module through explicit functional recovery. Finite freeness enters the dual base-change step. PairedModule supplies a perfect pairing, and PairedBimodule separately supplies balance and symmetry.
